children: By Mike Scarcella and David Thomas

US law firm Duane Morris has agreed to resolve a lawsuit that accused the firm of misclassifying some of its employees as partners in a bid to force them to pay part of the firm's taxes and expenses while denying them a share of its profits.
The firm and plaintiff Meagan Garland said in a filing in federal court in California on Wednesday that they reached an accord after mediation and were hashing out the terms.
Duane Morris had no immediate comment, and a lawyer for Garland did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Garland, who was previously a partner in the firm's employment practice, filed the proposed class action lawsuit against Duane Morris in August 2024. She alleged the Philadelphia-based firm was misclassifying its non-equity partners as "partners" even though they can be hired and fired at-will, and do not have an ownership stake in the firm.

Many US law firms internally designate some partners as non-equity or "income" partners. Such partners typically earn far less than full equity partners, whose compensation is tied directly to firm profits. Several major law firms in recent years have created non-equity partnership tiers.

After promoting lower-ranked lawyers to its non-equity partner tier, Duane Morris ceases paying the employer's share of their federal and state payroll taxes, as well as their benefits such as health care, vision, dental and disability insurance, Garland alleged.

Duane Morris in a court filing had denied any wrongdoing and said Garland was a "genuine partner whom the firm has always compensated and otherwise treated fairly and well within the bounds of the law."
US District Judge Cathy Ann Bencivengo in San Diego last year denied the law firm's bid to dismiss most of the claims in the lawsuit.
The case is Meagan Garland v. Duane Morris, LLP, et al., US District Court for the Southern District of California, 3:24-cv-01783
For Meagan Garland: Bibianne Fell and Marlee Horwitz of Fell Law
For Duane Morris: Anthony Oncidi, Gregory Knopp, Philippe Lebel and Elise Bloom of Proskauer Rose
